added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken; supplemental: the reviewed run's two gate arms (gate-head.log 2 passed, gate-existing.log 58 passed) each report no FAILED id, so no test regressed; the only FAILED line in the run directory is the intentional negative control.

findings.text: follow-on: read_plan maps to "reckon roadmap --project <project>", a command that answers a roadmap read rather than the read_plan call that timed out, so a computing read_plan timeout is pointed at work it did not ask for; the reviewed run's own manifest follow_on states read_plan has no CLI counterpart, so the code and its report disagree about the same mapping and a coordinator must decide whether read_plan names no command or the plan HTML path.

follow-on: assert "reckon" in result["hint"] does not verify the CLI-command half of the deliverable -- the word "reckon" is present in the base computing hint text ("this is a reckon work deadline") regardless of cli_command, and the test never asserts the mapped command string -- so dropping cli_command for every label would leave both tests green.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against the base; 570b7c40c adds _thread_cpu_seconds (a /proc reader) and _cause_of_timeout, threads them through _run_under_deadline, and adds the cpu_seconds/cause/cli_command fields on StorageSlowResult, while 4ecc70307 records the landing fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py; I re-ran it at head 4ecc703 -- 2 passed EXIT=0 (spinning body computing at about 0.2s CPU against 0.25s wall, sleeping body waiting at about 0.0s CPU) -- and independently reproduced the negative control in a scratch tree with _thread_cpu_seconds returning 0.0, which keeps the spinning case red (1 failed 1 passed EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a reckon MCP timeout names whether the abandoned body was computing or waiting; reckon/mcp.py:290 _cause_of_timeout and reckon/mcp.py:362 _run_under_deadline deliver it from the worker thread's CPU seconds read beside the wall time.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names commits 570b7c40c and 4ecc70307, the three gate logs and the negative control, but its follow_on states read_plan has no CLI counterpart while reckon/mcp.py:303 maps read_plan to a command, so the report contradicts its own diff.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff --name-only 72525a3 4ecc703 lists reckon/mcp.py, reckon/_mcp_tools.py, tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py and docs/evidence/fragments/an-mcp-failure-names-its-cause/mcp-timeout-names-its-cause.html, every one inside the manifest's declared paths; the declared docs/figures directory was correctly left unused.

justifications.durability: the assertions at tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py:45 and :61 name the regression that reddens them (the negative control shows the computing case reports waiting once the CPU measurement is zeroed) and :50/:65 pin cpu_seconds against a constant rather than a value the test passed in; the hint's CLI command is unguarded, because :55 asserts a substring present regardless of cli_command.
justifications.evidence: the gate tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py:45,:54,:61 measures exactly what the done_when asserts and its result is recorded in gate-head.log (2 passed EXIT=0) with the negative control in gate-negative-control.log (EXIT=1), both reproduced independently; the CLI-command half of the deliverable has no real assertion (see the finding on tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py:55).
justifications.fit: _cause_of_timeout and the _CLI_ANSWER_COMMANDS map follow the module's private-helper idiom at reckon/mcp.py:258-310 with no plan or version label; the pre-existing per-call state dict at reckon/mcp.py:363 is named waiting yet now also carries the worker tid and CPU baseline used to detect computing.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp.py:362 _run_under_deadline reports cause from the worker thread's CPU seconds read at reckon/mcp.py:410 beside the wall time, carries cpu_seconds/cause/cli_command on the result and leaves the error value storage-slow, meeting the deliverable; the read_plan CLI command named at reckon/mcp.py:303 does not answer read_plan's own work, so that clause is met only in part.
justifications.reuse: no owner of a thread-CPU reading exists (a search of reckon/ for /proc/self/task, time.thread_time or SC_CLK_TCK finds only mountinfo/cgroup readers) and no label-to-CLI map exists, so _thread_cpu_seconds and _CLI_ANSWER_COMMANDS introduce capability rather than fork one.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff 72525a3..4ecc703 sits inside reckon/mcp.py, reckon/_mcp_tools.py, tests/test_mcp_deadline_names_its_cause.py and the evidence fragment declared in the manifest, with no plan or shared-index write.
